prompt:
We need the deployable architecture package for the Cedar Rapids platform refresh, not a narrative design document. Build the stdlib-only `vcf_architecture` Python package in this repository and check in the architecture artifacts it generates.

The target is a greenfield VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0.0.0 deployment. Treat `fixtures/design-requirements.json` as the capacity, host-failure, network, and two-site recovery brief. Emit `artifacts/greenfield-sddc-spec.json` as an actual `SddcSpec` accepted by the pinned VCF Installer OpenAPI document at `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`; it is the upstream file from tag `9.0.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`. Model vCenter, SDDC Manager, NSX, and Fleet Manager as new deployments, keep ESX thumbprint and gateway-ping validation enabled, and define a distributed switch that covers every primary-site network with at least two distinct physical-uplink mappings. Keep deploy-time credentials as obvious `${SECRET_NAME}` placeholders, never real secrets.

Emit the cross-site capacity and availability decisions in `artifacts/site-architecture.json`. At the top level, include the `schemaVersion` string `1.0`, the source `requirementsId`, `targetVersion`, the complete `recovery` object, and a `sites` array. For each input site, preserve `siteId`, `role`, `hostFailureTolerance`, `hostProfile`, `minimumUsableAfterFailures`, and `networks`; report `hostCount`, `rawCapacity` across all hosts, and `usableAfterHostFailures` after the tolerated failures. Capacity objects cover `cpuCores`, `memoryGiB`, and `rawStorageTiB`.

There is also a live 5.2.1 estate to move. Its complete component inventory is `fixtures/estate-inventory.json`. Produce `artifacts/migration-plan.json` in `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`, with one ordered entry for every inventory component. Each entry must name the current component and version, its target component and version, its complete version path or replacement path, its technical compatibility gates, and its dependencies. `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json` is the pinned grading authority because the vendor matrices change; do not silently substitute newer live results for it. In particular, do not invent an in-place 9.0 upgrade for a product whose published path ends before 9.0.

Before designing the migration, use your own network research tools to consult current, reachable Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, upgrade-path, and VCF 9 upgrade-order sources. Search choices and URLs are up to you. Record what you actually consulted in `artifacts/research-sources.json`. The JSON object must contain an offset-aware ISO 8601 `researchedAt` timestamp and a `sources` array. Give each source its `publisher`, `title`, HTTPS `url`, nonempty `usedFor` decision list, and one or more `sourceTypes` chosen from `compatibility`, `interoperability`, `upgrade-path`, and `upgrade-order`; cover all four source types across the record. The pinned snapshot is not a substitute for this live research. The offline verifier checks the record without fetching its URLs.

The package builder must deterministically generate `greenfield-sddc-spec.json`, `site-architecture.json`, and `migration-plan.json`; the checked-in research record is provenance for those decisions rather than fixture-generated output. `python3 tests/verify_architecture.py` is the acceptance command. It first validates the checked-in SddcSpec against the pinned installer schema, then checks the package-generated architecture against the protected requirements, inventory, migration schema, compatibility snapshot, and research-record contract. Do not change the verifier, schemas, specification, fixtures, or package manifest.
